blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — visitor respiratory screening
stem: Why may a hospital use respiratory-symptom screening or related entry measures for visitors during periods of increased community respiratory-virus activity?

options.A: To help identify potentially infectious visitors and apply source-control or visit guidance as one part of layered respiratory-infection prevention.
options.B: To replace hand hygiene, ventilation, respiratory hygiene, and other prevention measures once visitors have been screened at the entrance.
options.C: To determine whether a visitor has a bacterial rather than viral illness, because viral respiratory symptoms do not affect visitor precautions.
options.D: To permanently exclude symptomatic visitors regardless of visit urgency, recovery, current transmission conditions, or facility risk assessment.

rationale: A is correct. Current CDC healthcare guidance recommends layered measures for viral respiratory pathogens. During higher community respiratory-virus activity, facilities can use screening/triage procedures, advise symptomatic visitors to defer non-urgent routine visits until recovered, and use source control and other infection-prevention measures. Screening is therefore one component of a layered approach. B incorrectly treats screening as a replacement for other controls. C falsely limits relevance to bacterial disease. D overstates visitor restrictions as permanent and non-contextual.
educational_objective: Explain that visitor respiratory-symptom screening helps identify potentially infectious persons and supports layered prevention of respiratory-pathogen introduction and transmission.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC); NCSBN
source_document_title: Preventing Transmission of Viral Respiratory Pathogens in Healthcare Settings; Infection Control Guidance: Respiratory Viruses; 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan
source_version_date: CDC healthcare respiratory-pathogen guidance dated May 21, 2025 and live-rechecked 2026-08-21; 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan effective April 2026
source_locator: CDC Preventing Transmission, sections 1-3: during increased community respiratory-virus activity, facilities may use rapid screening/triage; visitors with respiratory symptoms should be encouraged to defer non-urgent routine visits until recovery; masking/source control, hand hygiene, respiratory hygiene, separation, ventilation and other controls remain layered measures. Project Firstline: implement screening/triage procedures during higher community transmission and separate symptomatic persons promptly.
source_claim_supported: Current CDC guidance directly supports respiratory screening/triage and symptomatic-visitor guidance as components of layered infection prevention rather than substitutes for other controls.
blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control, printed p.8: apply infection-prevention principles, assess the care environment, and educate clients/others on infection-prevention concerns.
pdf_visual_verification: PASS — official 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan Safety and Infection Prevention and Control page was screenshot-verified earlier in this continuation; clinical claims rely on current CDC HTML.

option_audit.A: Correct; accurately reflects screening as one layered prevention tool.
option_audit.B: Plausible administrative-control overreach but screening does not replace other infection-prevention measures.
option_audit.C: Plausible diagnostic framing but screening is not limited to bacterial infections and viral symptoms are directly relevant.
option_audit.D: Plausible exclusion policy but CDC guidance is contextual and specifically mentions deferring non-urgent routine visits until recovery.

cueing_audit.answer_length: Options are comparable in detail and structure; the key is not uniquely signaled.
cueing_audit.absolute_words: No distractor depends on simplistic always/never/only wording.
